fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Outbound sync can only write to one tracker project, and it fails closed on anything else. Both
create transports take their project from a single construction-time value — Cloud
`AcliClient.create_issue` uses `self.jira_project` (`adapters/jira/acli.py:274-330`); DC
`_IssuesMixin.create_issue` uses `self.project` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py:163-189`). And
the applier scans every outbound mutation pre-flight and raises `CrossProjectTargetError` — aborting
the whole pass — if any update or delete targets a key outside the one configured project
(`applier.py:230-255`, `_cross_project_targets`, bug `626d`); its sole caller (`applier.py:593-610`)
passes a single string `select_backend(load_config()).project`. With a mapping listing several
projects, correct mutations to the other projects would be treated as the misconfiguration that guard
exists to catch.

## Approach

Three changes: resolve the create target per ticket (covering BOTH transports), relax the guard to
set membership, and change the guard's caller to supply the set.

**Create targets the ticket's resolved project — resolved once, above both transports.** The
resolution happens where the create mutation is BUILT, in `_compute_outbound_create_mutation`
(`outbound_differ.py:502`), which already receives the full local `ticket` (so it can read
`bridge_project`). It calls `resolve_project(ticket, mapping)` (`projects_store.py:97-110`) against
the store mapping, loaded once via `projects_store.load_mapping(repo_root)` (the `Mapping` that `resolve_project`
and the `mapping.projects` membership check both require) and threaded into
`compute_outbound_mutations` as a new optional field on `OutboundDiffConfig`, populated by that
function's sole caller `run_differs.py:466` (which already holds `repo_root`). Three outcomes:
  * resolves to "not synced" (absent→no legacy_default, or explicit `""`) → NO create mutation;
  * resolves to a key **NOT in `mapping.projects`** → NO create mutation (a stale/typo binding must
    not create against an unsynced project — this closes the create-side gap the guard cannot, since
    creates are guard-exempt: their key is a local-id placeholder, so `_JIRA_KEY_RE` never matches);
  * resolves to a valid in-set key → stamped into the mutation's `fields` under the reserved key
    `_bridge_target_project`.

Because the create mutation's `fields` reach whichever `TicketTransport` is active
(`dispatch_one.create_one` copies `mutation["fields"]` into the `ticket_data` it hands
`client.create_issue`), resolving here covers Cloud AND Data Center from one site. Each transport
reads `ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project")` and falls back to its construction-time value when
the key is absent (legacy single-project behaviour preserved): Cloud
`project = ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project") or self.jira_project`; DC
`fields.setdefault("project", {"key": ticket_data.get("_bridge_target_project") or self.project})`.
The transports handle the reserved key explicitly, because they treat unknown payload keys
DIFFERENTLY. Cloud's `create_issue` EXTRACTS only the fields it names and ignores the rest, so the key
never reaches ACLI. DC's `create_issue` splats the whole TRANSLATED dict into
`self._client.create_issue(**fields)` — so the key must be DROPPED before the splat or it is sent as a
bogus Jira field id (the `HTTP 400 … Field … cannot be set` class of bug 18a5). It is added to
`_BRIDGE_ONLY_CREATE_FIELDS` (`_issues.py:29`) alongside the bridge-only names `title`/`ticket_type`,
so `_translate_create_fields` reads it for the project then drops it — that drop is what keeps the
reserved key off the tracker by construction, exactly as the bridge-only names already are.

**The guard relaxes from equality to set membership.** `_cross_project_targets` currently compares
each target key's prefix against one `configured_project` string; it instead checks membership in the
mapping's project set. This is the smallest possible weakening: the guard stays fail-closed and still
aborts pre-flight before any tracker write, so a stale binding pointing at a project the store does
not sync is caught exactly as today. Only keys the store legitimately owns now pass.

**The guard's caller supplies the set.** The sole caller (`applier.py:593-610`) currently computes a
single `_project = select_backend(load_config()).project`. It instead loads the store's project set
via `projects_store.read_projects(repo_root)`, whose keys ARE the project set, and passes that set. An
empty/absent mapping falls back to the single configured project so single-project stores are
unchanged.

**Module size.** All touched files stay under the 800-line gate with headroom; each edit is small and
local.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` — resolve + validate + stamp the target
  project on the create mutation; new optional `OutboundDiffConfig` mapping field
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/run_differs.py` — populate the new config field from the loaded
  mapping (the sole caller of `compute_outbound_mutations`)
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira/acli.py` — Cloud create reads the payload target
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_issues.py` — DC create reads the
  payload target AND drops the reserved key in `_translate_create_fields`
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` — guard set-membership + caller supplies the set
- Read-only dependency: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/projects_store.py` — `load_mapping`/`Mapping`,
  `resolve_project`, `read_projects` (the authoritative project set)
- tests under `tests/`

## Testing

Tier per the shared standard's external-service row: a stateful fake transport fed production-shaped
mutations, recording the create calls it receives, because the destination project carried on the
call is the contract under test. Both transports are covered.

- Happy path (both transports): a ticket resolving to project `B` in a store whose mapping lists `A`
  and `B` produces a create call carrying `B`, not the repo default `A` — asserted against the Cloud
  fake AND the Data Center fake.
- DC leak guard: the DC fake's recorded create fields do NOT contain `_bridge_target_project`,
  proving the reserved key is dropped and never sent as a Jira field.
- Validation edge: a ticket whose `bridge_project` names `Z` (NOT in the `A`/`B` mapping) emits no
  create mutation — proving a stale/typo binding cannot create against an unsynced project.
- Contrast case (the guard, both directions in one paired test): an update targeting `B-1` where the
  mapping lists `A` and `B` proceeds; an update targeting `C-1` still raises `CrossProjectTargetError`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An outbound create targets the ticket's resolved project rather than the client default on the
      Cloud transport; checked by a Cloud fake asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [x] An outbound create targets the ticket's resolved project on the Data Center transport; checked
      by a DC fake asserting the project on the recorded create call.
- [x] The reserved `_bridge_target_project` key is dropped from the DC create field set; checked by
      asserting it is absent from the DC fake's recorded create fields.
- [x] A ticket whose resolved project is absent from the mapping set emits no create mutation;
      checked by asserting an empty mutation list for it.
- [x] An update inside the configured set proceeds while one outside it raises
      `CrossProjectTargetError`; checked by a paired test covering both directions.
- [x] When the guard raises, no tracker write has occurred; checked by asserting the fake recorded
      zero writes.
- [x] Single-project behaviour is unchanged; checked by a regression test running the guard against a
      one-project mapping in both directions.
